A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MuPT research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparison supports reliable assessment; pages 2–22 are visually identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-training experiments, scaling-law fits, objective music evaluations and human preference results in Section 4, plus ablations and early-stopping analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results, including the scaling-law comparisons in Table 3, music evaluations in Tables 4–5 and supplementary analyses in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The MuPT architecture, SMT-ABC synchronization procedure, tokenizer and SMS Law formulation in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same monophonic/polyphonic ABC corpus and symbolic-music generation tasks, including first-bar-conditioned evaluation. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Scaling-law comparisons retain Chinchilla, Data-Constrained and the same intermediate variants. Music evaluations retain GPT-4, MMT and the same ground-truth/random controls in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendices C–D retain identical data subsets, model configurations, context lengths, training budgets, evaluation metrics, fitting procedures and listening-test design.

E4.justification: The context-length and SMT-ABC comparison in Figure 4, scaling-law diagnostics in Figures 5–7, activation-function ablation in Table 6 and early-stopping analysis in Table 7 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank testing and significance reporting in Section 4.3.3 and Table 5 are identical. Neither version adds or removes seed, repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting information relative to the other.

E6.justification: All reported results and plotted curves match, including the SMS Law test R-squared of 0.9612 and Huber loss of 0.0028 in Table 3. Music-evaluation results and Appendix A result entries are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The scaling-law definitions and derivations in Section 3.4 and Appendix A, and the L-BFGS mathematical exposition in Appendix B, are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about long-context MuPT models, SMT-ABC, symbolic-music scaling and model releases.

C2.justification: Interpretations of musical structure, data repetition, scaling behavior and overfitting are unchanged, as are qualifications concerning limited data and unequal track lengths.

D1.justification: Tokenizer and preprocessing details, Appendix C hyperparameters, Table 8 training-token/time/GPU information and Appendix D assessment instructions are identical. Access links and their destinations also match.

R1.justification: Related work, references and positioning relative to MIDI-based models, earlier ABC-based research and existing scaling laws are unchanged.

P1.justification: The title page removes Jie Fu's M-A-P affiliation, changing the affiliation superscripts from 1 and 3 to 3 alone. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; all research prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–8 retain identical displays, captions and placement. The document layout is unchanged apart from the title-page text edits recorded under P1.

improvement.justification: v4 changes only an author-affiliation entry and the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, mathematical development, reproducibility information and presentation throughout the main paper and appendices remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
